Families across Papua New Guinea’s Highlands are facing depleted harvests and the threat of hunger after the El Niño weather pattern brought frost and prolonged dry conditions that have destroyed food gardens providing sustenance and income for thousands of households.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: 'Without the UK on board, the EU has integrated more'
rfi.description: Ten years after Britons voted to leave the European Union, the United Kingdom is more divided, less economically dynamic and no more influential on the global stage than Brexit supporters once promised. But for the EU, the consequences of the its departure may not have been entirely negative, says Federico Fabbrini of dedicated research centre, the Brexit Institute.

rfi.title: France bakes under heatwave as warnings extend into July
rfi.description: France was sweltering under another day of extreme heat on Wednesday after recording its hottest day on record – with millions under red alerts, schools closed, power cuts affecting tens of thousands of homes and ministers warning that another spell of exceptional temperatures could last until 14 July.

rfi.title: South Africa beat South Korea to reach World Cup knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Thapelo Maseko scored mid way through the second half against South Korea to take South Africa into the knockout stages at a World Cup for the first time.

rfi.title: Digital euro wins key EU backing as lawmakers approve draft rules
rfi.description: The European Union has moved a step closer to creating a digital euro, after members of the European Parliament passed a crucial vote on the virtual currency.

rfi.title: France announces first Ebola case in doctor returned from DR Congo
rfi.description: French health authorities on Wednesday announced the first confirmed case of Ebola identified on national territory – a doctor who had returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

rfi.title: Brazil overpower Scotland to take Group C as Morocco wear down Haiti
rfi.description: Brazil outclassed Scotland 3-0 on Wednesday night in Miami to claim Group C at the 2026 World Cup. Carlo Ancelotti's men started the final round of games in pole position following their 3-0 win over Haiti on 19 June while Morocco edged past Scotland 1-0.

rfi.title: US releases experimental Ebola drug for DR Congo outbreak trials
rfi.description: Experimental Ebola drugs are being shipped to Democratic Republic of Congo as the United States releases doses of a treatment for clinical trials in a widening outbreak that has caused more than 1,000 cases and over 250 deaths, the World Health Organization and US officials have said.

rfi.title: Switzerland outwit Canada to claim Group B at 2026 World Cup
rfi.description: Switzerland claimed top spot in Group B at the World Cup on Wednesday following a 2-1 win over Canada in Vancouver.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: 'The average British citizen has lost over £3,000 a year'
rfi.description: Ten years after the UK voted to leave the European Union, Brexit remains deeply divisive, with supporters and critics still at odds over its political and economic legacy. As part of RFI’s series marking the 10th anniversary of the referendum, we spoke to politics and international relations professor John Barry, one of its staunchest opponents.

rfi.title: Seven European countries urge ‘immediate halt’ to Sudan violence
rfi.description: Seven European countries have called on Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to immediately stop their assault on El-Obeid, a city in Sudan's North Kordofan state, warning of credible signs that a major offensive could be imminent as civilians face worsening shortages of food, water and fuel.

rfi.title: France scrambles to respond, as June heatwave grips Europe
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to hold a crisis meeting on Tuesday, after Météo France reported that the country's average temperature had broken a June record. Elsewhere in Europe, several countries are also struggling with the heatwave, which has led to a number of deaths and disruption to public services.

rfi.title: Portugal delays handover of French mother accused of abandoning children
rfi.description: Portuguese authorities have refused to immediately extradite to France a 41-year-old woman suspected of abandoning her two young children, who were found last month crying at the side of a road south of Lisbon.

rfi.title: Ghana dig in for stalemate with England at World Cup
rfi.description: Ghana fought their way to a 0-0 draw with England on Tuesday night that took them closer to qualifying for the knockout stages at the World Cup for the first time since their dazzling run to the last eight in 2010 in South Africa.

rfi.title: Resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch enters Paris's Pantheon
rfi.description: French resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch was inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on Tuesday in a sombre ceremony, giving President Emmanuel Macron another chance to shape France’s national memory through one of the country’s most symbolic events.

rfi.title: French government begins disciplinary action over child abuse case failings
rfi.description: The French government has announced disciplinary action against a magistrate and two gendarmerie officers over the handling of a suspect in child abuse case, which has lead to public outcry. This comes on the heels of a report which pointed to serious failings of the justice system, particularly with regards to minors.

rfi.title: Kenya halts US Ebola facility, health minister apologises for disobeying orders
rfi.description: Kenya has ordered a halt to preparations for a controversial US-run Ebola quarantine facility, the health minister told a court Tuesday, after being held in contempt for ignoring a previous stop-work order. The project has prompted widespread anger, and several people were killed during protests earlier this month.

rfi.title: EU gambles on Taliban talks to fast-track Afghan deportations
rfi.description: A Taliban delegation is due to fly into Brussels on Tuesday, having been granted a one-day visa to hold talks with the EU on returning failed asylum seekers to Afghanistan. However, human rights groups have warned that the scheme runs counter to the bloc's values.

rfi.title: Mbappé's double on 100th appearance fires France into World Cup knockout stages
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé marked his 100th cap for France on Monday night with two goals in their 3-0 win over Iraq in a game that took more than four hours to complete due to thunder storms over Philadelphia.

euronews.title: 7.1 and 7.5 magnitude quakes strike Venezuela causing what officials described as 'severe damage'
euronews.description: Residents of the capital Caracas were forced to evacuate their residences and seek shelter outdoors as the quakes, which struck less than 200 km from the capital, shook buildings and caused what President Rodriguez described as “severe damage”.

euronews.title: What is extreme heat stress? Inside the deadly phenomenon surging across Europe
euronews.description: Parts of Europe are witnessing up to 40 additional days with strong heat stress compared with the 1970s, according to a major new study.

euronews.title: Hormuz confusion deepens as Iran and US clash over who controls it
euronews.description: Trump said Tehran had promised no tolls or charges in the strait, hours after Iran and Oman announced a joint permit system asserting their authority over the waterway. Rubio flew to Abu Dhabi to reassure Gulf allies, as analysts warned control over Hormuz would be a major strategic victory for Iran

euronews.title: Deadly Hantavirus outbreak should end on 2 July, WHO says
euronews.description: The WHO says it will continue working with local authorities to investigate the causes and spread of the outbreak.

euronews.title: 'OpenLux' investigation reveals new Luxembourg firms linked to wealthy Spaniards
euronews.description: The international investigation 'OpenLux' uncovers new companies linked to some of Spain's biggest fortunes, including Amancio Ortega's property holding firms worth over €10 billion.

euronews.title: Catholics walk barefoot in mud ritual
euronews.description: Devotees in rice paddies cover themselves in mud and banana leaves for the Taong Putik festival, honouring St. John the Baptist with barefoot processions.

euronews.title: Scientists find human DNA over 2,000 years old in caves in Spain and Portugal
euronews.description: A research team based in Cáceres has found human DNA more than 2,000 years old on cave walls in Spain and Portugal, a discovery that could transform the study of prehistory.

euronews.title: Has Brexit made Europe stronger or weaker? MEPs go face-to-face on The Ring
euronews.description: What has Brexit taught Europe about sovereignty, migration, economic competitiveness, democratic accountability, and disinformation? Has it strengthened the case for deeper European integration? MEPs debate the future of EU-UK relations on this edition of The Ring.

euronews.title: UK records hottest June day ever as Europe swelters in heatwave
euronews.description: The Met Office has warned that "exceptionally warm" temperatures are expected to continue through the middle of the week.

euronews.title: Europe's five largest military powers meet ahead of key NATO summit with Ukraine in mind
euronews.description: The leaders of Europe's largest military powers met in Berlin on Wednesday in preparation for a pivotal NATO summit next month, to discuss support and security guarantees for Ukraine and how to strengthen the Atlantic Alliance's European Pillar.

euronews.title: German authorities carry out raids over alleged Russian gas sabotage
euronews.description: An investigation is looking into the sale of Gazprom's Berlin-based subsidiary Gazprom Germania, which took place around a month after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

euronews.title: Special Report: Brexit, ten years on: could the UK ever rejoin the EU?
euronews.description: Today's Special Report is anchored by Mared Gwyn and features correspondents Maria Tadeo and Shona Murray, alongside top interview guests, for a deep dive into one of the most consequential political decisions in modern European history: Brexit and the United Kingdom's departure from the EU.

euronews.title: IMF to closely monitor China’s economic growth amid trade tensions
euronews.description: An accurate measurement of China's digital economy is a priority for other powers competing with Beijing in fast-developing technologies.

euronews.title: London's Met police to scale up use of drones and live facial recognition
euronews.description: UK civil liberties campaign group Big Brother Watch has criticised the use of technologies such as drones and facial recognition.

euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this June 24th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Portugal's World Cup victory sparks celebrations in Lisbon
euronews.description: Thousands of fans in Lisbon celebrated Portugal's 5-0 World Cup victory over Uzbekistan, with Cristiano Ronaldo scoring twice and becoming the first player to score in six different World Cup tournaments.

euronews.title: Tourists disappointed as Eiffel Tower closes amid heatwave
euronews.description: Tourists have been left feeling disappointed as popular tourist attractions such as the Eiffel Tower and Louvre have shut early due to extreme heat.

euronews.title: Paris's Cirque d'Hiver begins renovation to restore its original splendour
euronews.description: Twenty ornamental frescoes from the Second Empire are to be restored over twelve to eighteen months. The seating, the polychrome ceiling canvas and the stained-glass windows will also be refurbished.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump exploite les célébrations du 250ᵉ anniversaire des Etats-Unis pour s’autocélébrer
lemonde.description: Le président a donné le coup d’envoi des festivités, mercredi soir, à Washington, lors d’un rassemblement aux allures de meeting de campagne, dans une approche qui assimile le patriotisme américain au culte de sa personne.

lemonde.title: Après avoir enregistré sa journée la plus chaude, la France entraperçoit la fin de la canicule
lemonde.description: Avec une moyenne jour-nuit à 30 °C, le 24 juin a établi un nouveau record de chaleur en France. Les prévisionnistes escomptent une sortie progressive de la canicule d’ici à dimanche, dans l’Ouest. La chaleur persistera jusqu’à mardi 30 juin ou mercredi 1ᵉʳ juillet dans le reste du pays.

lemonde.title: Au Venezuela, deux puissants séismes font craindre un bilan « lourd » et des dégâts « importants »
lemonde.description: Une première secousse de magnitude 7,2 est survenue vers 18 heures, suivie d’une autre, 39 secondes plus tard, de magnitude 7,5 et 45 km plus loin. Des immeubles se sont effondrés dans la capitale, Caracas. L’état d’urgence a été déclaré par la présidente, Delcy Rodriguez.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : l’enquête visant Jérôme Barella élargie aux qualifications de meurtre et de viol sur mineur
lemonde.description: L’autopsie n’a pas permis de déterminer « avec certitude » la cause de la mort de l’enfant de 11 ans, a annoncé, mercredi 24 juin, le parquet d’Agen dans un communiqué.

lemonde.title: L’interdiction des mariages d’étrangers sans papiers de retour à l’Assemblée nationale, avec le soutien du gouvernement
lemonde.description: La proposition de loi, portée par l’UDR d’Eric Ciotti, répond à la demande de quelques maires qui refusent de célébrer des unions qu’ils soupçonnent être frauduleuses, sans intention matrimoniale. « Le Monde » est allé à la rencontre de personnes qui se sont heurtées à de telles fins de non-recevoir.

lemonde.title: Les syndicats de SFR redoutent des milliers de suppressions de postes après le rachat du groupe par Bouygues, Orange et Free
lemonde.description: Les représentants du personnel de SFR ne sont pas sortis rassurés d’une réunion avec les directeurs généraux de Bouygues Telecom, Free et Orange, mercredi 24 juin.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Volodymyr Zelensky donne l’ordre de mener des frappes « préventives » contre des installations russes
lemonde.description: Dans un post diffusé mercredi soir sur Telegram, le président ukrainien a annoncé avoir demandé aux services de renseignement ukrainiens et à l’armée ukrainienne « d’agir de manière préventive contre ⁠des ‌installations que la Russie utilise pour ​étendre son effort de guerre ».

lemonde.title: Aurélien Rousseau quitte la campagne de Raphaël Glucksmann
lemonde.description: Le député des Yvelines sort de l’équipe du fondateur de Place publique, pour des raisons personnelles. Il n’est, à ce stade, pas remplacé à ce poste.

lemonde.title: CNews : la mise en demeure de la chaîne d’informations par l’Arcom est une « décision politique », juge Maxime Saada, le patron de Canal+
lemonde.description: Le président du directoire du groupe Canal+, dans le giron de Vincent Bolloré comme CNews, dénonce, dans une tribune publiée dans « Le Figaro », une décision visant à « faire taire (…) une chaîne que des millions de Français choisissent librement ». CNews a été épinglée pour son manque de respect du pluralisme à l’antenne.

lemonde.title: En Turquie, l’énorme désillusion face au parcours catastrophique de l’équipe nationale au Mondial
lemonde.description: Les autorités affichaient de grandes ambitions pour l’équipe nationale et en avaient fait un outil de propagande. La réalité du terrain les a rattrapées.

lemonde.title: Biarritz : une plongeuse meurt après l’effondrement d’un pan de falaise près d’une plage ; un autre plongeur disparu
lemonde.description: Trois plongeurs se trouvaient au pied de la falaise au moment de la catastrophe survenue vers 20 h 20, mercredi, l’un d’eux ayant pu s’en sortir indemne. Les recherches ont été suspendues peu avant minuit.

lemonde.title: Guerre en Iran : l’administration Trump demande au Congrès une rallonge de près de 88 milliards de dollars pour faire face aux dépenses dues au conflit
lemonde.description: Le Pentagone se verrait attribuer à lui seul plus de 67 milliards de dollars pour éponger les « coûts opérationnels » de la guerre et « reconstituer les stocks de munitions ».

lemonde.title: Trois juges de la CPI visées par des sanctions américaines portent plainte contre Donald Trump et son administration
lemonde.description: Les trois magistrates accusent le président américain, le secrétaire d’Etat, Marco Rubio, et le secrétaire aux finances, Scott Bessent, d’« exercer une pression extrajudiciaire ». Une mesure de rétorsion, selon elles, aux mandats d’arrêts délivrés par la Cour pénale internationale contre Benyamin Nétanyahou.

lemonde.title: Un portrait d’Amedeo Modigliani vendu 56 millions d’euros établit un nouveau record européen pour une œuvre du peintre italien
lemonde.description: Le tableau « Nu assis au collier » a été cédé, mercredi à Londres, dans le cadre de la vente aux enchères de la collection d’art de l’homme d’affaires britannique Joe Lewis.

lemonde.title: Les conclusions explosives des Assises du financement des universités : frais d’inscription multipliés par cinq, ouverture à la réduction du nombre d’étudiants…
lemonde.description: Le ministre de l’enseignement supérieur, Philippe Baptiste, souhaite qu’un débat s’ouvre sur ces sujets lors de la campagne présidentielle et estime qu’il « faut réfléchir à des mécanismes contributifs de la part des étudiants qui peuvent se le permettre ».

lemonde.title: Au Liban, le Hezbollah accuse Israël d’avoir violé deux fois le cessez-le-feu « en moins de quarante-huit heures »
lemonde.description: Deux personnes sont mortes dans une frappe israélienne, mercredi, près de la ville de Nabatiyé, dans le sud du pays. La veille, deux autres avaient été tuées dans le même secteur. L’Etat hébreu a affirmé dans les deux cas viser des « terroristes ».

lemonde.title: Donald Trump refuse de signer une loi sur le logement tant qu’un autre texte sur le droit de vote n’est pas adopté
lemonde.description: En visite au Capitole de Washington, le président américain s’est également confronté à des sénateurs républicains qui ont voté, mardi, une résolution symbolique pour ordonner le retrait des forces américaines de l’Iran.

zeit.description: Erdbeben haben in Venezuela Häuser zum Einsturz gebracht, Fachleute rechnen mit Tausenden Toten. Innenminister Cabello spricht von einer »alarmierenden Situation«.

zeit.title: Russland und der Ukrainekrieg: Jetzt spüren auch die Russen den Krieg
zeit.description: Drohnen, hohe Preise, kein Mobilnetz: Nach viereinhalb Jahren spürt die russische Bevölkerung die Folgen des Krieges gegen die Ukraine. Wird das für Putin gefährlich?

zeit.title: Elbvertiefung: Der tägliche Newsletter aus Hamburg: Warum Füchse Schuld daran sind, dass in Hamburg so viele Möwen brüten
zeit.description: Die Elbvertiefung am Donnerstag – Mit dem abgesagten Halbmarathon, vielen neuen Sparmaßnahmen der Stadt und einem weiteren toten Fahrradfahrer

zeit.title: Urlaub: Ferien mit Rad und Roman der Ehefrau - Minister auf Reisen
Donald Trump: Drill, baby, drill – der Anti-Klimaschutz-Präsident
zeit.description: Donald Trump betreibt eine systematische Schwächung der Klimaschutzpolitik. Unser Thema im US-Podcast. Außerdem: die Verhandlungen mit dem Iran und JD Vance’ Rolle

zeit.title: Crispy Jollof Rice: Wenn bei 30 Grad der Hunger kommt
zeit.description: Essen kann in der Sommerhitze schwierig sein. Dieses knusprige westafrikanische Reisgericht ist frisch, spritzig, sättigend – und liegt ganz federleicht im Magen.

nzz.title: Zwei schwere Erdbeben erschüttern Venezuela: Präsidentin Rodríguez ruft den Notstand aus – Viele Tote befürchtet
nzz.description: Innerhalb weniger Minuten richteten zwei Erdbeben in Venezuela verheerende Schäden an. Rettungskräfte suchen unter den Trümmern nach Überlebenden. Über das Ausmass der Schäden ist noch kaum etwas bekannt.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Live-Daten zeigen: So nahe steht die Schweiz am Hitzerekord
nzz.description: Hitzetage und Tropennächte sind deutlich häufiger geworden. Dieser Trend wird sich fortsetzen. Besonders in den Städten kühlt die Luft kaum mehr ab. Die neusten Zahlen zur Hitze in der grafischen Übersicht.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Von Mamdani bis Meyer/Wermuth: Die Gen-Z-Sozialisten kapern die Sozialdemokratie
nzz.description: Der unrühmliche Abgang von Daniel Jositsch war erst der Anfang. Junge Linke krempeln die alten sozialdemokratischen Parteien um – nicht nur in der Schweiz, sondern weltweit. Ihr Treibstoff: Hass auf Israel und Reiche.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ AKZENT» - Andy Burnham: Kann der «König des Nordens» Grossbritannien stabilisieren?
nzz.description: Mit der Rücktrittserklärung von Keir Starmer verabschiedet sich der sechste britische Premierminister – innerhalb von zehn Jahren. Ein neuer steht in den Startlöchern. Kann er das Land aus der Krise führen?

nzz.title: Prämien für Babys: Indien läutet eine radikale Wende in der Bevölkerungspolitik ein
nzz.description: Während Jahrzehnten bekämpfte Indien die Bevölkerungsexplosion mit Sterilisationen und Familienplanung. Doch in den letzten Jahren ist die Geburtenrate massiv gesunken. Nun wollen indische Politiker gegensteuern. Kritiker warnen vor unerwünschten Folgen.

nzz.title: Murat Yakin coacht Jesse Marsch aus – aber der Eindruck der Schweizer Fussballer an dieser WM bleibt zwiespältig
nzz.description: 2:1 gegen Kanada, Gruppensieg, lange Erholung vor dem Sechzehntelfinal: Das Nationalteam hat geliefert. Doch einen Zweifel vermag Murat Yakins Equipe nicht zu zerstreuen – er hat mit den Einwechselspielern zu tun.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Böses Blut um historische Symbole: Polen und die Ukraine kämpfen an der falschen Front
nzz.description: Der Streit um die leidvollen Ereignisse im Zweiten Weltkrieg läuft immer mehr aus dem Ruder. Präsident Selenski hat deswegen sogar seinen Besuch in Polen abgesagt. Nun sollten kühlere Köpfe obsiegen, denn die beiden Nachbarn sind existenziell aufeinander angewiesen.

nzz.title: Lecornu führt Drogentests für Minister und hohe Beamte ein
nzz.description: Drogenskandale erschüttern die politische Klasse Frankreichs. Nun greift der Regierungschef Sébastien Lecornu zu drastischen Massnahmen.

nzz.title: Hitzewelle in Europa: warum es schon im Juni so extrem heiss ist und weshalb sich die glühende Luft so lange hält
nzz.description: Über Westeuropa hat sich eine Hitzeglocke aufgebaut. Vor allem in Frankreich herrschen rekordhohe Temperaturen. Dazu haben mehrere Faktoren beigetragen.

nzz.title: Leroy Sané macht es seinen Kritikern leicht. Einer ist ihm treu ergeben: Julian Nagelsmann. Zu Recht?
nzz.description: Der deutsche Nationalspieler hat seine Aufgaben an der WM passabel erledigt. Aber von einem Spieler seines Formats erwartet man mehr.

nzz.title: «Ein Vehikel für Schwarzgeld»: Professoren greifen den Trinkgeld-Entscheid des Ständerats an
nzz.description: Der Ständerat setzt sich für die Gastronomie ein und will Trinkgelder von Steuern und AHV-Beiträgen befreien. Arbeitsrechtsexperten warnen vor einem Missbrauch durch Handwerker, Coiffeure, Boten.

nzz.title: Die grosse Rätselgestalt der Literatur: Wer war Ingeborg Bachmann wirklich?
nzz.description: Als Schriftstellerin war sie eine Meisterin der Mehrdeutigkeit. Aber ihr Leben war auf einen unerfüllbaren Wunsch ausgerichtet: dass es klare Verhältnisse gibt. Vor 100 Jahren wurde Ingeborg Bachmann geboren.

nzz.title: Mit der falschen Regeneration bringt das härteste Training nichts. Und das Schlimmste ist, zu wenig zu essen
nzz.description: Auch dank ihm hat Jonas Vingegaard zweimal die Tour de France gewonnen. Der Ernährungswissenschafter Martijn Redegeld gibt Tipps, die Amateuren wie Profis helfen.

nzz.title: Das Bally-Rätsel: Bis auf die Marke ist fast nichts mehr da – wie geht es weiter?
nzz.description: Seit Jahrzehnten reichen sich Finanzinvestoren die traditionsreiche Schuh- und Modefirma weiter. Nach der Schliessung der Produktion im Tessin ist unklar, was der heutige Besitzer vorhat.

nzz.title: Vor 50 Jahren wurde das Meme erfunden – wie das Internetphänomen entstanden ist
nzz.description: Memes sind im Internet omnipräsent und entsprechend wirkmächtig. Sie werden von Politikerinnen und Politikern im Wahlkampf eingesetzt und neuerdings sogar als Kunst gehandelt. Warum sind diese oft humorvollen Bilder und Videos derart erfolgreich?

nzz.title: Das berühmte italienische Dreirad Ape kehrt als Stromer zurück und heisst nun Tris: So will Fiat die Erfolgsgeschichte fortschreiben
nzz.description: Die Ape war Symbol des Wirtschaftswunders, der Tris ist ein modularer Kunststoffbaukasten aus Marokko. Ist er ein würdiger Nachfolger – oder nur ein Retromobil für sonnige Tage?

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: La Suisse passe devant le Maroc à Vancouver, les Haïtiens héroïques battus par les Marocains qui se qualifient pour les les seizièmes de finale derrière le Brésil. Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Afrique du Sud se qualifie et envoie la Corée du Sud en salle d'attente
Mondial 2026 : l'Afrique du Sud se qualifie en 16es et envoie la Corée du Sud en salle d'attente
france24fr.description: Le groupe A de la Coupe du monde a rendu son verdict. Si le Mexique a parachevé sa domination en venant à bout de la République tchèque, l'Afrique du Sud a quant à elle renversé la vapeur pour arracher la deuxième place du groupe, synonymes de 16es de finale. Son adversaire, la Corée du Sud, attendra de voir si elle sera repêchée.

france24fr.title: 250 ans des États-Unis : Donald Trump lance les festivités avec un discours politique
france24fr.description: Sans beaucoup s'étendre sur les principes de la déclaration d'indépendance du 4 juillet 1776, le président américain Donald Trump a vanté son bilan et étrillé ses prédécesseurs lors d'un discours donné mercredi soir, au cœur de Washington, pour lancer les festivités des 250 ans des États-Unis.

france24fr.title: État d'urgence au Venezuela après deux puissants séismes qui laissent craindre un lourd bilan
État d'urgence au Venezuela après deux puissants séismes qui font craindre un lourd bilan
france24fr.description: L'état d'urgence a été déclaré au Venezuela, frappé coup sur coup mercredi soir par deux séismes de magnitudes 7,2 et 7,5. Plusieurs immeubles se sont effondrés dans la capitale Caracas où des scènes de panique ont eu lieu. L'aéroport international, gravement endommagé, est fermé. Les experts craignent un lourd bilan, et les États-Unis de Donald Trump se sont dits prêts à aider leurs "nouveaux et formidables amis".

france24fr.title: En direct : la Maison Blanche demande 88 milliards, "en grande partie" pour la guerre en Iran
france24fr.description: La Maison Blanche a demandé mercredi au Congrès américain une rallonge budgétaire de près de 88 milliards de dollars, dont "la plupart" doivent répondre à "des besoins urgents" liés à la guerre en Iran. Donald Trump a remis en question une implication de l'armée américaine dans le bombardement meurtrier de l'école iranienne de Minab, qui a tué plus d'une centaine d'enfants au premier jour de la guerre au Moyen-Orient fin février. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le Maroc s’en sort face à un Haïti historique, le Brésil en tête du groupe C
Mondial 2026 : le Maroc s'en sort face à un Haïti historique, le Brésil en tête du groupe C
france24fr.description: Le duel à distance pour la première place du groupe C entre le Maroc et le Brésil a tourné à l'avantage de la Seleçao. Les Lions de l'Atlas l'ont emporté sur des Haïtiens déjà éliminés mais héroïques (4-2) tandis que les quintuples champions du monde ont battu les Écossais (3-0) sans forcer. Les deux équipes filent en 16es de finale mais à la différence de but, c'est le Brésil qui finit en tête du groupe.

france24fr.title: AfSud - Corée du Sud : revivez la qualification des Bafana Bafana
france24fr.description: Groupe A de la Coupe du monde, suite et fin. L'Afrique du Sud a réalisé un exploit face à la Corée du Sud pour se qualifier en 16es de finale. Revivez le match historique grâce au live commenté de nos confrères de RFI.

france24fr.title: Une conférence sur l'Ukraine s'ouvre à Gdansk, en Pologne, sans Volodymyr Zelensky
france24fr.description: La ville polonaise de Gdansk accueille jeudi et vendredi responsables politiques et acteurs économiques pour discuter de la reconstruction de l'Ukraine après la guerre avec la Russie. La délégation ukrainienne sera conduite par la Première ministre Ioulia Svyrydenko et non le président Zelensky, en raison des récentes tensions entre Varsovie et Kiev.

france24fr.title: Canicule : l'Europe du Sud s'organise, la France improvise
france24fr.description: La France n'est pas seule dans cette fournaise. L'Europe est touchée depuis plusieurs jours par des pics de chaleur mais certains pays s'en sortent mieux que d'autres. Cela fait plusieurs années déjà qu'ils ont mis en place des dispositifs pour permettre aux travailleurs et aux écoliers de faire face, au mieux, à cette chaleur écrasante à laquelle il va falloir s'habituer.

france24fr.title: La climatisation est-elle diabolisée à tort, comme l'affirme le Rassemblement National ?
france24fr.description: Après des années à critiquer la réalité du réchauffement climatique et notamment les rapports du GIEC, le Rassemblement National dénonce aujourd'hui l'impréparation du gouvernement et prône comme solution unique la climatisation généralisée des bâtiments, affirmant qu'elle serait diabolisée à tort. En réalité, le bilan environnemental de cette technologie est beaucoup plus complexe que ne le laissent entendre certains responsables politiques. Info/Intox fait le point.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Suisse finit en tête du groupe B, le Canada qualifié et la Bosnie en ballottage
Mondial 2026 : la Suisse finit en tête du groupe B, le Canada qualifié et la Bosnie repêchée
france24fr.description: La Suisse s'est imposée 2-1 face au Canada et termine première du groupe B. Une déception pour les Canadiens qui rêvaient de l'emporter à Vancouver et disputer un 16ème de finale historique sur leur sol. La Bosnie s'est quant à elle imposée 3-1 face au Qatar et est déjà assurée de finir parmi les meilleurs troisièmes.

france24fr.title: Maroc - Haïti : les Lions de l'Atlas qualifiés après un long combat
france24fr.description: Groupe C, suite et fin. Le Maroc affrontait Haïti à Atlanta pour sécuriser la première place du groupe C, dans un duel à distance avec le Brésil qui jouait l'Écosse au même moment. Qui a finalement basculé en tête de la poule ? Revivez les deux matches à travers notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Guy Stéphan, de l'ombre de Deschamps, à la lumière
france24fr.description: Le sélectionneur de l'équipe de France Didier Deschamps est rentré en France pour assister aux obsèques de sa mère. En son absence, ​son adjoint ​Guy Stéphan ​va diriger vendredi la rencontre contre la Norvège, décisive pour ​la première place du groupe. Les deux hommes travaillent en duo depuis 17 ans.

france24fr.title: La justice tunisienne confirme la peine à 8 ans de prison de la militante anti-raciste Saadia Mosbah
france24fr.description: En Tunisie, la militante anti-raciste Sadiaa Mosbah a vu sa condamnation de prison être confirmée en appel mardi 23 juin selon ses avocats. Elle avait été arrêtée le 6 mai 2024, accusée de malversations financières avec d'autres membres de son association Mnemty qui lutte contre la discrimination raciale.

spiegel.title: Neuer Literatur-Newsletter: Wie kann der Bachmann-Preis gutes Fernsehen sein?
News: WM-Spiel Deutschland gegen Ecuador, Friedrich Merz, schwarz-roter Rentenkompromiss, Organspenden
spiegel.description: Kanzler Merz ist verzaubert vom Spiel seiner Mannschaft, die Linke stolpert in die Regierungsunfähigkeit und der Bundestag debattiert über Organspenden. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Süßstoffe: Wie gefährlich Aspartam wirklich ist – ein Ernährungswissenschaftler klärt auf
spiegel.description: Sie sollen das Mikrobiom verändern, zu Heißhunger führen oder sogar krebserregend sein: Sind Zuckeralternativen wie Aspartam wirklich so schlecht wie ihr Ruf? Das sagt der Ernährungswissenschaftler.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Bundestrainer Julian Nagelsmann hält nichts von Rotation gegen Ecuador
spiegel.description: Bundestrainer Julian Nagelsmann will nicht zu viel wechseln. Brasiliens Superstar Neymar steht wieder auf dem Platz. Und: Gastgeber Mexiko spielt eine perfekte Gruppenphase. Das sind die WM-News des Tages.

spiegel.title: Polizei in Offenburg beendet »anstößiges Schauspiel« im Burgerwaldsee
spiegel.description: Ein Paar ist sich im baden-württembergischen Burgerwaldsee nah gekommen. So nah, dass Badegäste die Polizei riefen. Die Beamten berichten nun über ihren »ungewöhnlichen Einsatz«.

spiegel.title: Australien: Studie zeigt, wie Jugendliche das Social-Media-Verbot austricksen
spiegel.description: Seit Ende 2025 sind in Australien die meisten sozialen Medien für Kinder unter 16 Jahren gesperrt. Jetzt liegen erste Zahlen zu den Auswirkungen vor. Sie sind ernüchternd.

spiegel.title: Fotos zeigen Zerstörung in Caracas
spiegel.description: Die starken Erdbeben in Venezuela brachten Häuser zum Einsturz und lösten vielerorts Panik aus. Aufnahmen aus der Hauptstadt Caracas lassen das Ausmaß der Schäden erahnen.

spiegel.title: Veronica Ferres ist in die Oscar-Akademie eingeladen
spiegel.description: Schauspielerin Veronica Ferres darf künftig mit darüber abstimmen, wer den begehrtesten Filmpreis der Welt erhält. Sie ist nicht die einzige Deutsche, die ein Angebot der Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences erhielt.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Brasilien schlägt Schottland - Ist die Boston Beer Party jetzt vorbei?
spiegel.description: Schottische Fans tranken Bostons Biervorräte leer, ihre Mannschaft hatte im Duell mit Brasilien nichts zu feiern: Sie trödelte und machte Fehler. Ob es Schottland noch in die K.-o.-Runde schafft, entscheidet die Konkurrenz.

spiegel.title: Doppel-Erdbeben in Venezuela – schwere Schäden, viele Menschen verschüttet
spiegel.description: In Venezuela hat nur kurz hintereinander zweimal die Erde gebebt. Die US-Erdbebenwarte USGS rechnet mit vielen Toten, erste Opfer sind bestätigt. Die Regierung in Caracas hat den Notstand ausgerufen.

spiegel.title: Rente: Die Verhandlungen hätten fast die Koalition gesprengt. Plötzlich ist sie ihr größter Coup
spiegel.description: Bei der Rente ist der Koalition gelungen, was ihr kaum einer zugetraut hat: ein Kompromiss. Und der wird auch noch von fast allen gelobt. »Es muss schnell gehen«, fordert nun Kanzler Merz. Doch es gibt einen Haken.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump kritisiert Friedrich Merz und lobt Wolodymyr Selenskyj
spiegel.description: Kurz vor dem Nato-Gipfel in Ankara hat Donald Trump die fehlende Unterstützung durch Deutschland im Irankrieg angeprangert – und überraschend warme Worte für die Ukraine gefunden.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Marine stopft Risse am Wrack des 1999 untergegangenen Öl-Tankers »Erika«
spiegel.description: Vor rund 26 Jahren ist der Tanker »Erika« vor der Bretagne gesunken – mit katastrophalen Folgen für die Umwelt. Noch immer lagert Schweröl in den Wrackteilen. Nun wurde ein schwieriger Einsatz in der Tiefe nötig.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump streitet mit der eigenen Partei und brüllt Senator an
spiegel.description: Im Disput um ein verschärftes Wahlrecht erpresst Donald Trump seine Republikaner. Er will ein anderes Gesetz so lange blockieren, bis er seinen Willen bekommt. Ein Mittagessen mit Senatoren aus den eigenen Reihen ist nun eskaliert.

spiegel.title: VW verkauft Motorentochter für 7,4 Milliarden Euro
spiegel.description: Der ‌US-Finanzinvestor Bain Capital übernimmt die lukrative VW-Tochter Everllence. Das Unternehmen stellt Schiffsantriebe und Generatoren her. Der Verkauf an den amerikanischen Investor gilt als Überraschung.

spiegel.title: Bundeswehr: Fast 300.000 Fragebögen zum Wehrdienst verschickt – 530 Freiwillige für 2026 rekrutiert
spiegel.description: Das Verteidigungsministerium meldet positive Zahlen zum Start des neuen freiwilligen Wehrdienstes. Rund 96 Prozent der Männer hätten auf den Fragebogen der Bundeswehr reagiert. Den übrigen drohen Sanktionen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Manzambi führt Schweiz gegen Kanada zum Gruppensieg
spiegel.description: Im zweiten Spiel saß Johan Manzambi erst nur auf der Bank, ehe er nach seiner Einwechslung zwei Tore schoss. Nun durfte der Freiburger Offensivspieler gegen Kanada erstmals beginnen. Und führte die Schweiz zum Gruppensieg.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Zwei Mitarbeiter von Minenräumorganisation bei Angriff getötet
spiegel.description: Russischer Beschuss hat nach ukrainischen Angaben zwei Mitarbeiter der Hilfsorganisation Norwegian People's Aid getöte. Diese setzt ihre Einsätze vorerst aus, aber warnt vor zunehmenden Gefahren für humanitäre Helfer.

phys-org.title: Shorter front-leg strides can be an early warning sign of dementia in senior dogs
phys-org.description: Scientists have shown that the stride length of the front legs (but not the hind legs) of senior and geriatric dogs decreases as their cognitive performance worsens. In contrast, chronological age itself was a poor predictor of stride length. A similar reduction in step length has been well documented in people with dementia. These results suggest that a decline in stride length could be an early warning sign of canine dementia, and so an informative new tool for veterinarians.

phys-org.title: Precious drops: Spray helps crop farmers facing declining rainfall
phys-org.description: A spray made from a biodegradable polymer capable of capturing and redirecting water to crop seeds could be the key to drought-proofing Western Australian farms.

phys-org.title: Designer proteins unlock near-infrared and SWIR glow for deeper tissue imaging
phys-org.description: Researchers at the National Center for Tumor Diseases (NCT/UCC) in Dresden, including Oliver Bruns and Dr. Bernardo Arús, are participating in an international study that has, for the first time, developed novel proteins for near-infrared (NIR) and short-wave infrared imaging (SWIR). The research was conducted in collaboration with an international team that included chemistry Nobel laureate David Baker, who was honored in 2024 for his work on computational protein design. The study, with shared

phys-org.title: Ancient stories inform modern understanding of volcanic eruptions
phys-org.description: A new international study has found that Indigenous oral traditions, some thousands of years old, hold valuable and often overlooked insights into volcanic eruptions—offering important lessons for modern disaster preparedness. The research, published in the journal Volcanica, was led by Museums Victoria Research Institute volcanologist Dr. Heather Handley and draws on case studies from Australia, Fiji, Hawai'i, Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands and Vanuatu to demonstrate how Traditional

phys-org.title: 'Fingerprints' of black hole's event horizon detected for first time
phys-org.description: Scientists have detected the "fingerprints" of a black hole's event horizon—the boundary from which nothing can escape—for the first time, according to research published Wednesday.

phys-org.title: 'Super-puff' planets lighter than candy floss discovered by international team
phys-org.description: An international collaboration has discovered two of the lowest-density giant planets ever detected: rare "super-puff" planets with densities lower than candy floss. The study—led by the University of Oxford, in collaboration with Université Côte d'Azur/Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur and the University of Birmingham—has been published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.

phys-org.title: Pesticide widespread in blood of French Indies adults: Study
phys-org.description: Eight in 10 adults in the French West Indies have a toxic pesticide in their blood decades after banana growers stopped using it, a study said Wednesday.

phys-org.title: Did gravitational tides cause Earth's extinctions?
phys-org.description: Life on Earth took a long evolutionary journey that eventually created us, the purportedly intelligent species that dominates the planet. But there was no grand plan or design, only happenstance, nature and luck. Life on Earth suffered multiple extinctions, but got up, dusted itself off and continued on its long march to complexity.

phys-org.title: Laser experiments push helium to record shock pressures
phys-org.description: Deep inside gas giants like Jupiter and Saturn, hydrogen and helium coexist under pressures millions of times greater than Earth's atmosphere. Under those conditions, helium may separate from hydrogen and influence a planet's internal heat flow, structure and magnetic field. Understanding these processes and how these materials behave under extreme conditions is essential to building accurate models of planetary evolution.

phys-org.title: How longer exciton lifetimes could ease efficiency trade-off in organic solar cells
phys-org.description: Although the efficiency of organic solar cells has now risen to more than 20%, there are physical limits that make it difficult to further increase their performance. A research team from Linköping University in Sweden, the University of Potsdam, the Paul-Drude-Institut in Berlin and other collaborators has now demonstrated which physical processes limit a key parameter in the performance of organic solar cells. This opens up the possibility of overcoming the long-standing efficiency limits of o

phys-org.title: Mathematical modeling helps advance use of magnetic particles in targeted drug-delivery systems
phys-org.description: A Florida State University computational scientist is paving the way for future medical breakthroughs by developing mathematical models and simulations to predict the behavior of a unique drug-delivery method, which aims to deploy treatments directly to targeted sites in the body.

phys-org.title: Drifting tuna gear creates risks for wildlife in protected marine areas
phys-org.description: An international study co-authored by a University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa researcher has found that drifting devices used by the global tuna fishing industry are entering marine protected areas around the world, creating potential risks for wildlife and sensitive ocean habitats.

phys-org.title: Web archive lets you easily search millions of government documents
phys-org.description: At the end of every presidential term, the End of Term Web Archive preserves that administration's web presence as a vast trove of documents and webpages. The archive began in 2008, with George W. Bush's second term, and runs through 2024, collecting images, text, graphs, redacted pages and other media. So while it contains important public information, finding that information in the glut can prove difficult.

phys-org.title: A magnetic field that kills superconductivity can also bring it back
phys-org.description: Magnetic fields are generally known to destroy superconductivity in a material. However, in exceptional cases, they can lead to what is known as "re-entrant superconductivity"—where superconductivity disappears as expected, but then unexpectedly returns when the magnetic field is increased further.

phys-org.title: Euclid mission view of Milky Way's heart previews upcoming survey by NASA's Roman
phys-org.description: A new look at the heart of our Milky Way galaxy by Euclid, an ESA (European Space Agency) mission with NASA contributions, overlaps with a region scientists will observe with NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, launching later this summer. This sneak peek gives astronomers a major jumpstart on a core Roman survey, helping scientists learn more than they could from either telescope alone.

phys-org.title: X-ray snapshots reveal how viral shells change shape as they dry out
phys-org.description: When viruses travel through the air in tiny droplets, they can quickly start to dry out. Yet many viruses remain infectious after rehydration—something that is still not fully understood. Now, an international team of researchers has directly observed at the European XFEL how the protein shells of viruses can change shape during dehydration, offering new clues to viral resilience and opening new possibilities for virology research. phys-org.title: Free love in communes? Not quite, says researcher
phys-org.description: The myth of the sexually liberated life of communes is persistent, even though research shows a different reality. According to postdoctoral researcher Anna Heinonen of the University of Eastern Finland, the idea that roommates would have very free sexual relationships with each other is a strange concept in modern commune living.

phys-org.title: What happens when environmental change outpaces life's ability to adapt?
phys-org.description: When an animal's environment changes faster than the animal can adapt, its chances of survival can flatline. The same is true for populations and even entire species. Now, scientists at MIT and the University of Leicester have found that this connection between evolutionary adaptation and the pace of environmental change holds up at the global scale as well—and can determine life's susceptibility to mass extinction. new-sci.title: Possible signs of ancient life on Mars are rich in complex carbon
new-sci.description: An instrument on the Perseverance rover has identified large, complex carbon compounds alongside unusual patterns on the surface of rocks that resemble traces of microbial activity

new-sci.title: Screwworm could be the first species targeted by an 'extinction drive'
new-sci.description: We have developed genetic technologies that could wipe out entire species of pests that are harmful to us. Columnist Michael Le Page says the flesh-eating screwworm is the most likely first target

new-sci.title: All known Homo naledi skeletons seem to be female
new-sci.description: An analysis of tooth proteins suggests all 23 Homo naledi individuals found in the Rising Star cave in South Africa were female, which strengthens the case that they were placed there deliberately

new-sci.title: The lunar botanist with a plan to farm vegetables on the moon
new-sci.description: Jessica Atkin knows more than anyone else about what it would take to supply food for a moon base. She reveals how to build a lunar farm and what astronauts can expect to dine on

new-sci.title: Some of the last Neanderthals were surprisingly genetically diverse
new-sci.description: Genetic analysis of Neanderthals in north-western Europe reveals that this population was surprisingly genetically diverse, hinting that inbreeding didn’t lead to the species' demise

new-sci.title: Fluctuating oestrogen levels may alter how drugs enter women's brains
new-sci.description: Oestrogen levels fluctuate throughout a woman's menstrual cycle, which may impact how efficiently a drug that targets the brain can reach its destination

new-sci.title: Hidden black hole could explain mystery at the heart of our galaxy
new-sci.description: The area surrounding our galaxy’s central supermassive black hole contains three strangely different populations of stars – but one hidden black hole could explain all of them

new-sci.title: You should turn off fans when it's too hot – but how hot is too hot?
new-sci.description: Fans can make you hotter rather than cooler, but the temperature at which you should turn them off depends on several factors, including your age and the humidity level

new-sci.title: Huge crater in Australia may be the oldest impact structure on Earth
new-sci.description: A study claims that the North Pole Dome crater in Western Australia was caused by an asteroid strike 3 billion years ago, but other researchers dispute the proposed age

new-sci.title: Elite Maya people had teeth placed in a cave far from their tombs
new-sci.description: A cave in Belize contains teeth from dozens of important Maya people buried elsewhere, which may attest to a ritual intended to ensure their passage to the underworld

new-sci.title: Parenting may permanently improve brain health for mums and dads
new-sci.description: Raising children appears to keep the brain young, potentially acting as a buffer against cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s

new-sci.title: SpaceX's secretive plans to deliver cargo to Earth from space
new-sci.description: Not much is known about Starfall, SpaceX's new delivery system, but an assessment published in May revealed its intended purpose

new-sci.title: How some people's brains make an extraordinary recovery from stroke
new-sci.description: Around a third of people are able to almost fully rebuild their brains after a stroke and uncovering why is pointing the way to better treatments for everyone

new-sci.title: Unapproved gene therapy for boosting longevity is set to go on sale
new-sci.description: A gene therapy that instructs cells to produce more of an anti-ageing protein called klotho is about to be offered by a US company at overseas clinics to bypass FDA rules

new-sci.title: Woman with Alzheimer's starts conversing again after taking psilocybin
new-sci.description: A woman with severe Alzheimer's disease who hadn't spoken more than monosyllables in years began initiating conversation after a single dose of psilocybin

new-sci.title: New-to-science spider builds trap that flings ants into the air
new-sci.description: A spider living in the rainforests of Queensland, Australia, builds a snare trap reminiscent of a Roman-era ballista weapon that it uses to catapult green tree ants into a web 30 centimetres above

new-sci.title: How menopause radically changes the brain – and what happens after
new-sci.description: The brain undergoes a full renovation during menopause. Although these changes are profound, we’re learning that the long-term impact needn’t be all bad

new-sci.title: ‘Fusogenic’ neurosurgery let paralysed pigs walk again – are we next?
new-sci.description: Researchers say a surgery that let pigs with completely severed spinal cords walk again may lead to human trials, and then perhaps even full head or brain transplants. Columnist Helen Thomson is intrigued but sceptical of whether the technique can be successful in humans

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.
